root_cause.text: The tracing trigger free path in `trigger_data_free()` mishandled the `trigger_data_free_list` when the cleanup kthread could not be created, queuing boot-time `event_trigger_data` objects but later freeing only the current object instead of draining previously deferred list entries, leaving stale queued nodes and leading to a crash.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that “boot-deferred nodes can accumulate on `trigger_data_free_list`, later frees fall back to synchronously freeing only the current object, and the older queued entries are leaked forever,” and the patch fixes this by adding `trigger_data_free_queued_locked()` and calling it when `kthread_create()` fails and in the late-init path so the whole deferred list is drained.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor trigger data cleanup by adding locked helper routines for conditional kthread creation and synchronized freeing of queued event_trigger_data objects.
intent_record.what: The change adds a forward declaration for trigger_kthread_fn() and introduces two new static helper functions: trigger_create_kthread_locked(), which asserts trigger_data_kthread_mutex is held and conditionally creates the trigger_data_free kernel thread and stores it with WRITE_ONCE if creation succeeds, and trigger_data_free_queued_locked(), which asserts the same mutex is held, removes all nodes from trigger_data_free_list, returns if the list is empty, calls tracepoint_synchronize_unregister(), and frees each queued event_trigger_data entry with kfree().
intent_record.how: At runtime, this factors out and centralizes two pieces of behavior under the mutex: safe one-time creation of the background kthread and synchronized draining/freeing of queued trigger data. It enables callers to explicitly create the worker thread only when absent and to safely reclaim deferred event_trigger_data objects after waiting for tracepoint unregistration synchronization, reducing the risk of freeing queued data at the wrong time.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix trigger-data deferred freeing so early-boot kthread creation failures queue work safely and process it later or synchronously as a fallback.
intent_record.what: The change adds a boot-time special case in trigger_data_free() that queues event_trigger_data onto trigger_data_free_list and returns when the system is still booting and trigger_kthread does not yet exist. In the existing no-kthread path, it now acquires the mutex, calls trigger_create_kthread_locked(), and if the kthread is still unavailable it queues the item, drains queued frees synchronously with trigger_data_free_queued_locked(), and returns, instead of directly creating the kthread inline or falling back to tracepoint_synchronize_unregister() and kfree(data). It also adds a new __init function, trigger_data_free_init(), registered with late_initcall(), which under the same mutex checks for queued deferred frees, attempts to create the kthread, and either wakes it or synchronously drains the queued list if creation still fails.
intent_record.how: At runtime, deferred trigger-data freeing now survives early-boot cases where kthread creation is not yet possible or initially fails. During boot, frees are preserved on the lockless list instead of being forced down an immediate slow-path free, and later initialization will start the worker thread to process them. Outside boot, if worker creation still fails, the code now frees through the queued-drain path under locking rather than bypassing the deferred-free mechanism. This avoids losing deferred work semantics during boot and ensures queued frees are eventually processed either asynchronously by the kthread or synchronously as a fallback.

vuln_statements.explanation: This fallback free is the direct bug: when the cleanup kthread could not be created, previously deferred event_trigger_data objects had already been queued on trigger_data_free_list, but this path freed only the current object instead of draining the queued list, leaving stale list entries that later caused a crash.

This condition gates entry into the buggy fallback path used during early boot or kthread creation failure. Under this branch, the implementation mishandled deferred cleanup by not processing trigger_data_free_list.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it shows the full free-path logic in `trigger_data_free()` and the associated cleanup thread behavior. The vulnerable construct is present in the fallback path when the kthread cannot be created. Specifically, `trigger_data_free()` first attempts to lazily create the cleanup thread: `if (unlikely(!trigger_kthread)) { ... kthread = kthread_create(...); if (!IS_ERR(kthread)) WRITE_ONCE(trigger_kthread, kthread); }`. If creation fails, it takes the fallback path: `if (!trigger_kthread) { /* Do it the slow way */ tracepoint_synchronize_unregister(); kfree(data); return; }`. The root cause says previously deferred `event_trigger_data` objects may already be queued on `trigger_data_free_list`, but when the kthread is unavailable this code frees only the current `data` and returns. There is no code here to drain `trigger_data_free_list` in that fallback path. Meanwhile, the normal path does queue objects with `llist_add(&data->llist, &trigger_data_free_list); wake_up_process(trigger_kthread);`, and the kthread frees them via `llnodes = llist_del_all(&trigger_data_free_list); ... llist_for_each_entry_safe(data, tmp, llnodes, llist) kfree(data);`. Thus, if the kthread cannot be created after entries have been queued, the fallback does not clean up the existing list, matching the described bug. The fix is not present because there is no handling in the `!trigger_kthread` fallback to call `llist_del_all()` and free all previously queued entries along with the current one.
